keys.explanation: Wrong cleaning methods can create the contamination problem they aim to solve.
External high-power electrical and RF sources can couple into a campus environment.
Accidental EPO is a major outage cause; over-locking can also block emergency response.
Concentrated loads are point/small-area forces that can govern panel and pedestal design.
Cameras without response/integration are weak; alarm-linked video + NTP-aligned logs enable forensics.
Water versus energy is a classic plant design tension—site climate and policy drive choices.
Very low RH favors ESD risk; high RH raises condensation and corrosion concerns—hence humidity is managed with temperature.
Legacy myths fade, but strong local fields can still matter for certain gear, analog paths, and people.
Understructure integrity is foundational to access-floor safety and performance.
Gaseous agents can extinguish without wet-system water damage, with design-specific trade-offs.
External connectivity risk is as much pathway and carrier as interface speed.
Induced voltage in loops is the classic copper EMI mechanism at ELF.
Facility elements centre on power, cooling, space, connectivity, life safety, and security that enable IT operation.
Early warning converts latent water risk into actionable ops response.
Legal and landlord constraints can block critical plant rights even on otherwise attractive campuses.
EN 50600 is European-series awareness; ISO/IEC 22237 is the international facilities series awareness.
Vertical clearances constrain cooling architecture, cable plant, and equipment handling.
Dry outdoor air or dehumidifying coils can drop indoor moisture; humidification restores the site humidity control band.
Facility incidents cross subsystems; correlation beats siloed dashboards.
Sensible capacity removes heat at constant moisture; latent capacity addresses moisture. IT loads are mostly sensible.
Depth planning fails when cables, PDUs, and service clearances are ignored.
EN 50600 commonly appears in European project and procurement contexts.
Water-dependent cooling and fire protection make water rights and infrastructure first-class site criteria.
MTBF speaks to failure frequency/reliability; do not confuse with repair speed.
Real portfolios see mixed root causes—power, cooling, people, and environment—site by site.
Unit equipment carries local emergency power for required egress lighting duration.
WUE is a water-intensity metric relating site water use to IT energy.
Commissioning checks actual illuminance against design intent.
Perforated doors pass supply/exhaust air; solid doors belong with contained/chimney designs.
Three-phase distribution supports high kW delivery more effectively than single-phase alone.
Abort criteria and rollback are part of safe maintenance design.
Abort is a controlled investigation tool under procedure, not system abandonment.
Colo security is multi-tenant compartmentalization on top of site controls.
EMS here is environmental monitoring; clarify vs energy-management naming collision in interviews.
Blindness is itself a fault mode; dead sensors create false confidence.
Fault tolerance targets uninterrupted service through a worst-case single failure, not only planned maintenance windows.
Ceilings can organize services and airflow return—but plenum use must match listing and design intent.
N+1 means one spare relative to required module count.
Overstuffed pathways and tight bends damage performance and reliability of copper and fiber.

policy: e2e/harness and post-grade explanations only; not the learner exam payload
